title: Invited: Neuromorphic Vision Modalities in the NimbleAI 3D Chip
problem: Enabling novel passive monocular neuromorphic vision modalities with foveated and light-field event-driven vision that encode 3D visual surroundings as sparse events in a 4D spatiotemporal domain. The challenge is integrating these sensing modalities with processing circuitry and memory in a compact 3D-integrated silicon volume.
motivation: Neuromorphic event-driven vision with inherent 3D depth encoding enables efficient, miniaturized perception systems for edge AI applications.
method: The NimbleAI architecture uses 3D silicon stacking (stacking silicon layers vertically) to integrate a vision sensor, spiking neural circuits, and memory in one compact chip. The vision sensor captures sparse events (sudden changes in light) using light-field event-driven sensing (recording from multiple angles to infer 3D depth) combined with selective foveated attention (focusing computation on important regions), encoding data across four dimensions: horizontal position, vertical position, depth, and time. This sparse 4D encoding enables the architecture to efficiently execute standard computer vision algorithms on neuromorphic (event-based) inputs.
key_novelty: Combining light-field event-driven vision (capturing 3D depth from light-ray angles), selective foveated attention (focusing on important regions), and neuromorphic processing in a single 3D-stacked chip creates a compact, efficient architecture for 3D scene understanding.
contributions: Novel passive monocular neuromorphic vision modalities with foveated and light-field event-driven vision and selective visual attention
4D spatiotemporal sparse event representation of 3D visual surroundings as alternative to traditional Dynamic Vision Sensor outputs
Hardware architecture supporting efficient execution of mainstream computer vision and AI algorithms on neuromorphic visual inputs
3D silicon integration design for miniaturized sensing-processing co-integration
limitations: Not discussed - this is an overview of ongoing work without specific performance comparisons or evaluation metrics presented.
